newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELS FEELS TOP PLAYERS ANSWER WOODS'S CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS FEELS TOP PLAYERS ANSWER WOODS'S CHALLENGE.

text.p: U.S. Open champion Ernie Els feels the world's top players have answered the challenge of Tiger Woods emphatically -- by winning golf tournaments.
But the South African stressed that beating the sensational young American was not his particular aim in events where they both play.
Just when it seemed he was in a bit of a slump, Woods confirmed his talent on Sunday by winning the Western Open near Chicago -- his seventh triumph in just 10 months as a professional.
With the victory, he regained the top spot in the world rankings, with Greg Norman, Els and Colin Montgomerie right behind.
"Yes we have responded," Els said on Tuesday, on the eve of the Loch Lomond World Invitational.
"Just look at the last few weeks. I won the U.S. Open, Greg won in Memphis and on Sunday Colin won in Ireland," Els said.
"But we must not get away from the fact that playing the game of golf is not just about beating Tiger Woods," he added hastily.
"He's playing tremendous golf and he has one hell of a record already. But it is not us against Tiger or Tiger against us.
"It's us playing the game and trying to put the best score on the board. At least that's the bottom line as far as I'm concerned.
"My goal is to try and beat the golf course and the field, not just Tiger Woods," Els said.
Norman answered the same question by saying he did not react to a good player but to good play.
"When you get the best players playing together, a good player will always make another good player lift his game," Norman said.
Woods is not playing at Loch Lomond this week but the other three right behind him in the rankings are, as is world number six Tom Lehman, the reigning British Open champion.
